scienceworld_action.description: Execute one native ScienceWorld action. On the first call, this starts the current task variation automatically. Each phase is a single game attempt — no restart within a phase.

action.description: One textual action sent to the environment, for example `look around`, `open fridge`, or `mix beaker 1 with beaker 2`.

env_name.description: Target ScienceWorld task name. Required on the first call of a task.

variation_num.description: Target variation number for the current task. Required on the first call of a task.

task_index.description: Fallback task index used when `env_name` is omitted.

env_step_limit.description: Maximum step limit for the episode.

generate_gold_path.description: Whether to request a gold-path explanation from the runtime when supported.

server_path.description: Optional absolute path to the ScienceWorld server/JAR runtime.

query_wm.description: Query the current in-memory world model graph for this task session. Returns all discovered rooms, connections (action -> destination room), score changes, and untried actions per room (frontier). Use this to see where you have been, what you have tried, and what remains unexplored. No parameters needed.

wiki_memory_read.description: Search the wiki knowledge base using grep (literal string matching). Use this in Phase 2 to find relevant skills, world knowledge, and past experiences before or while solving a task.

query.description: Search string. Matched case-insensitively across all wiki .md files. Try keywords from the current observation, task goal, or objects you need to find.

section.description: Which wiki section to search: 'knowledge' (skills/tactics), 'experiences' (past lessons), 'world_model' (all locations+objects), 'locations' (rooms), 'objects' (items), or 'all' (default).

max_results.description: Maximum number of matching pages to return.

run_terminal_cmd.description: Execute a shell command. Use this in phase_m to read trajectory logs (head/tail/cat) and write wiki files (python3 -c for multi-line writes, mkdir for directories). Also useful for general file system operations.

is_background.description: Whether to run the command in the background.
